check_faq_sub: Everything you want to know about website performance and Google ranking.
check_faq_1_q: How fast should a website load?
check_faq_1_a: Google recommends that the LCP (largest element) loads within 2.5 seconds. Anything above 4 seconds is considered poor and harms your Google ranking.
check_faq_2_q: What is a good SEO score?
check_faq_2_a: An SEO score of 90 or higher is excellent. This means your website is technically well set up: good meta tags, alt text for images and a crawlable structure.
check_faq_3_q: What does the accessibility score mean?
check_faq_3_a: The accessibility score indicates how well your website can be used by people with disabilities — such as visually impaired users who use a screen reader. A higher score also helps your SEO.
check_faq_4_q: How do I improve my website speed?
check_faq_4_a: The most impactful improvements are: converting images to WebP format, removing unnecessary scripts, using fast hosting, enabling caching and minifying CSS/JS.
check_faq_5_a: Core Web Vitals are three official Google performance metrics: LCP (load time), TBT/FID (interactivity) and CLS (layout stability). They directly influence your position in search results.
